Okay, so I need to figure out if the action in the scenario is morally acceptable. Let me read through it again.

The person is a man who usually talks to Lois because she's been through a tough time since her husband died. Last time he saw her, she was talking with a couple of other people. He waved and gestured for her to call him instead of talking to her directly.

Hmm, so the main points are: he usually makes an effort to talk to Lois because she's going through a hard time. But last time, she was with others, so he didn't talk to her but instead gestured for her to call him.

I think the key here is whether his action was considerate or not. He didn't ignore her completely; he waved and gestured, which shows he noticed her. But he didn't approach her because she was with others. Maybe he didn't want to interrupt her conversation.

Is it wrong to not talk to someone because they're with others? I don't think so. It's considerate to not interrupt someone else's conversation. Plus, he made an effort to gesture for her to call him, which shows he still cares about her and wants to talk later.

So, his action was kind and considerate. He didn't completely ignore her, just chose a different way to communicate without interrupting her current interaction. That seems morally acceptable.
